parsed.explanation: Outing can trigger documented presentation arrests, disproportionate loitering/immorality detention, and an advocacy law read to cover gender-identity expression, with up to three years' imprisonment for same-sex conduct. Police sexual coercion, a 2023 cross-dressing conviction to civil prison, harsh custody, healthcare discrimination and impunity show the state as perpetrator and bystander, not protector. No execution or capital pathway is documented, and the 2015 capital-policing account is dated, so this sits above the 0.15 lethal-custody anchors but below 0.25 short-detention anchors.

entry_documents.exposure: Same-sex conduct criminalised up to 3 years; no legal gender-marker route is a resident gap, not counted, but presentation/document mismatch can provoke decency arrest.
entry_documents.protection: 2023 decree requires non-discriminatory passenger screening on sexual life/orientation; not stated to cover gender identity.
entry_documents.interaction: Border or police document check can convert mismatch into investigation under decency, loitering or advocacy provisions.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Arbitrary and disproportionate arrests, January 2021 imprisonment until an organisation paid release, 2023 civil-prison conviction, harsh prisons and arbitrary detention.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No operative visitor recourse documented; mistreatment tends to go unpunished.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for presentation, loitering or advocacy leads to the documented harsh, discriminatory custody environment.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No birth-sex bathroom, ward or custody-placement rule is documented; facilities risk is inferred only through general decency policing, not a universal facility ban.

care_services.exposure: HIV/STD providers discriminate against LGBTQ patients, causing care avoidance; prisoners denied HIV treatment and condoms; medication/confiscation for visitors not documented.
care_services.interaction: Discovery in care risks outing, stigma and denial, with no documented non-discrimination remedy for gender identity.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 393 criminalises same-sex acts; Article 392 criminalises LGBTQ advocacy, read by a 2023 report to reach gender-identity expression and enforced. 2018 and 2023 presentation arrests prove use against trans people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Article 5 bans homophobic defamation, not stated to protect gender identity or visitors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Sexuality law is not abstract here: neutral decency/loitering offences are the documented lever against gender-nonconforming people.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-specific documented rule; a guardian's outing could expose the family to the same general enforcement, but that is not sourced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Violence/threats against LGBTTQI people listed 2022-2023; November 2019 police followed a trans woman home and coerced sex, prevented only by her mother. 2015 capital account is dated.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No effective police protection documented; stigma and criminalisation deter reporting.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are documented perpetrators, so seeking help risks further exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Impunity, official/societal discrimination and lack of gender-identity anti-discrimination law; resident legal support exists but no visitor remedy is documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Limited defamation and screening provisions above; no documented complaint success.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper provisions do not offset documented enforcement, custody harm and non-reporting incentives.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: routine presentation arrests, illusory remedies and custody harm. Higher than 0.15 because no documented beatings campaign, months-long pretrial pattern or capital clause; worst documented custody is harshness and a 2023 civil-prison term.
Lower than 0.25: that anchor has rare imprisonment and fines/extortion; here statutory 1-3 years, repeated arrests and actual imprisonment are documented, plus police sexual coercion and impunity.

Materially lower than 0.35: that anchor involves stops, fines and release without imprisonment. Here prosecution and imprisonment are documented, police are sexual-coercion perpetrators, and recourse is not merely deferential but impunity-documented.

Far lower: 0.65 has explicit national protection, release and compensation after a document stop. Here there is no gender-identity protection, enforcement is against presentation, and no compensation or discipline is documented.

parsed.synthesis: Combined nationally, entry, police, decency, advocacy and custody rules form one punitive pathway: mismatch or visible presentation leads to stop, arbitrary detention or prosecution, in harsh conditions with discriminatory care and no effective complaint route. The 2023 screening/defamation provisions do not cover gender identity and are not shown operating for visitors. No subnational variation is measured; the capital account is dated. Absence of execution keeps this above 0.05-0.15 lethal anchors, but documented imprisonment, police-perpetrated coercion and impunity drive it to severe risk.
